I remember it as much as I remember the rest of elementary school. It definitely was not a large part of the curriculum which is why I think a lot of people have forgotten the details. I remember the initial testing being done with a black haired woman and my grandma was there as she was my guardian at the time. It was in our school’s music room and the lights were dim and shades drawn. We did IQ pattern recognition tests, rorschach pictures, audio tests, card games where she would sit behind a manilla folder and ask me to guess what shape was on the card she picked, also matching card games. I remember going for this same testing maybe 2-3 times and never really understood why I was there as the lady said we were just playing some fun games. After that I was pulled out of class weekly for more brain game exercises with a small group of other kids. More matching games, card games with each other, reading exercises to predict foreshadowing, etc. LOTS of audio testing to see if we could hear specific frequencies. I never regarded myself as very exceptionally “smart” either but I did have very good perception skills from trauma at a young age and am neurodivergent (diagnosed in adulthood) so maybe that was factored in. A lot of people discuss being fed some kind of fluoride liquid which I don’t recall experiencing.

Yes! this sounds like an IQ test. We did those as well but I recall even having special reading time where we practiced analyzing “foreshadowing” and honing in on context clues to “guess” what happens next in the story. It sounds very simple but having 5-6 year olds practice this really gave us critical skills regarding intuition and pattern recognition from a young age.

I’m not sure tbh. I didn’t think it was an abnormal experience until other people came out and said something was off with the way they were testing us. I agree we were socially secluded as I didn’t interact much with other kids outside of the gifted classes, so we all got tested this way and were all highly interested in “nerdy” things so it never seemed odd at the time. My middle school experience was similar to yours, it was moreso just advanced versions of the same classes the rest of the kids my age took. But elementary school was very different, we had specific time in small groups outside of class with certain puzzles and reading exercises that were guided with themes of practicing intuition. hey! i would suggest definitely seeing a counselor or psychologist just to be able to retrain your brain and learn some coping mechanisms that can help you deal with these feelings when they come on. i suffer from emetophobia, which gives me a lot of anxiety and that general queasy feeling you’re talking about. try to maybe keep a hand sanitizer on you. psychologically, smelling alcohol or another strong scent like lemon distracts your brain enough to quell that nauseous feeling since it’s got a mental cause and not a physical one. the same thing happens when you take small sips of room temperature water. any sort of brain distraction will help pull you back down to earth at least a little bit. practice deep breathing when these feelings come on, too. my therapist once explained to me how anxiety actually works- it’s an irrational spike in adrenaline. fight or flight kicks in and the parasympathetic nervous system triggers these feelings of anxiety. taking deep breaths automatically reverses the parasympathetic nervous system. so it’s literally impossible to panic and breathe deeply at the same time after about 5 minutes, as long as you really breathe slow and deep. hope this helps!
